# Test fixtures

Every fixture here is **synthetic**: invented conversations, tools, ids and model output, written in the formats the real clients and providers use. Nothing in this folder was recorded from a real session or account.

- `clients/`: requests in the shapes Claude Code and Codex CLI send (named after the client version whose format they follow), generated by `go run ./scripts/synth-clients`.
- `upstream/`: responses in the shapes NVIDIA build and Ollama return (JSON, SSE streams, error bodies), generated by `go run ./scripts/synth-upstream`.
- `analyze/`: session transcripts in the on-disk formats of Claude Code, Codex CLI and Antigravity (IDE and CLI stores), for the `cbrt analyze` adapters, generated by `go run ./scripts/synth-transcripts/<tool>`. Invented projects, prompts, tool calls and token counts.

Both generators are deterministic: running them again must leave the files unchanged. Edit the generators, not the files.

The analyzer adapters are also checked against your own stores with `go test -tags local ./internal/analyze/adapters/...`; those tests read your real transcripts, print counts only, and write nothing into the repository.

When a client or provider changes its format, look at its traffic **locally** (`cbrt record … -out captures/x`; `captures/` is git-ignored), then describe the new structure in the generator with invented content. Never copy text, ids or values from a recording.

Before pushing, run the privacy audit: `go test ./scripts/privacy`. It scans the whole repository for real-looking UUIDs, e-mail addresses, keys, user and temp paths and app names (UUIDs and keys only in `testdata/`), and, with a local git-ignored `.privacy-terms` file (one term per line), for your own terms, including terms split across stream fragments. CI runs the built-in checks on every push.
